concepts.name: Bow and arrow
concepts.summary: Storing muscle energy in a bent stave and releasing it through a string to shoot a light projectile fast and accurately.

concepts.name: Crossbow
concepts.summary: A bow fixed across a stock and released by a trigger, so that it can be held drawn and aimed and shot by a lightly trained soldier.

concepts.name: Firearms
concepts.summary: Using the gas pressure of burning gunpowder inside a tube to drive a projectile.

concepts.name: Nuclear weapon
concepts.summary: An explosive device that releases energy from a runaway nuclear fission or fusion reaction.

concepts.name: High explosives
concepts.summary: Chemical explosives that detonate far more violently than gunpowder and are set off reliably by a detonator.

concepts.name: Fortified settlement
concepts.summary: Enclosing a place where people live with walls, ditches or ramparts built to keep attackers out.

concepts.name: Bastion fort
concepts.summary: A low, thick-walled fort with angled projecting bastions that resists cannon fire and leaves no ground unswept by the defenders' guns.

concepts.name: Standing professional army
concepts.summary: A permanent body of soldiers kept, supplied and paid by a state all year round, not raised only for a campaign.

concepts.name: Mounted archer warfare
concepts.summary: Fighting from horseback with the bow, so that a force can strike and withdraw faster than any army on foot.

concepts.name: Mass conscription
concepts.summary: Obliging the men of a whole population to serve as soldiers by law, so that armies draw on the nation and not on a military class.

concepts.name: Operations research
concepts.summary: Using measurement, statistics and mathematical models to decide how equipment and forces should be used.

concepts.name: Cryptanalysis
concepts.summary: Systematic methods for reading enciphered messages without the key.

concepts.name: Public-key cryptography
concepts.summary: Encryption and signatures using a pair of mathematically linked keys, so that strangers can communicate securely without first sharing a secret.

concepts.name: Weighed metal as money
concepts.summary: Using a metal measured by standard weights as the common unit for prices, debts, wages and fines.

concepts.name: Coinage
concepts.summary: Pieces of metal of standard weight issued and marked by an authority so that they pass by count instead of being weighed.

concepts.name: Paper money
concepts.summary: Printed notes that circulate as money on the promise or authority of their issuer.

concepts.name: Bills of exchange and deposit banking
concepts.summary: Moving and lending money through written orders to pay and through transfers between accounts held with a banker, without carrying coin.

concepts.name: Mobile money
concepts.summary: Holding and sending money through a mobile phone account and a network of cash agents, without a bank branch.

concepts.name: Double-entry bookkeeping
concepts.summary: Recording every transaction twice, as a debit and a credit, so that the books balance and show profit and capital.

concepts.name: National income accounting
concepts.summary: Measuring the total output, income and spending of a whole economy in one consistent set of accounts.

concepts.name: Long-distance caravan trade
concepts.summary: Regular overland trade by organised pack-animal caravans that links distant economies across desert or steppe.

concepts.name: Marketplace system
concepts.summary: Regular public marketplaces where households buy and sell everyday goods at bargained prices using accepted means of payment.

concepts.name: Online commerce
concepts.summary: Buying and selling over a public computer network, with payment made securely at a distance.

concepts.name: Written law code
concepts.summary: A ruler's or community's rules and penalties set down in writing and published, so that judgments can appeal to a fixed text.

concepts.name: State census and taxation
concepts.summary: A government regularly counting people, land or herds and taking a set share of produce or labour from them.

concepts.name: Government by citizen assembly
concepts.summary: Public decisions and offices placed in the hands of the body of citizens meeting, voting and serving in turn.

concepts.name: Confederation by council
concepts.summary: A lasting league of self-governing peoples under a common council with agreed rules for deciding war, peace and disputes.

concepts.name: Representative assembly
concepts.summary: A standing body of delegates chosen by towns, districts or estates whose consent is needed for taxes and laws.

concepts.name: Patent system
concepts.summary: A general law granting inventors an exclusive right to their new devices for a limited term in return for making them known.

concepts.name: Social insurance
concepts.summary: Compulsory state-run insurance, paid for by contributions, that supports workers in sickness, injury and old age.

concepts.name: Joint-stock company
concepts.summary: A lasting enterprise whose capital is divided into shares that many investors own and can sell, with their risk limited to what they put in.

concepts.name: Scientific management
concepts.summary: Studying work by measurement and experiment, then setting methods, times and pay by plan instead of custom.

concepts.name: School
concepts.summary: A set place and curriculum where the young are taught in groups by appointed teachers, apart from learning at home or by apprenticeship.

concepts.name: Competitive examinations for office
concepts.summary: Choosing officials by open written tests of learning instead of by birth or recommendation.

concepts.name: University
concepts.summary: A self-governing corporation of teachers and students that teaches the higher branches of learning and grants recognised degrees.

concepts.name: Compulsory schooling
concepts.summary: A state requiring every child to attend school for a set number of years and providing the schools to make it possible.

concepts.name: Research university
concepts.summary: A university whose teachers are expected to make new knowledge and to train students by having them do research.

concepts.name: Scientific journal
concepts.summary: A periodical that prints dated reports of new findings under the oversight of a learned body, fixing priority and building a shared public record.

concepts.name: Critical history writing
concepts.summary: Reconstructing the human past by inquiry, weighing sources and explaining events by human causes.

concepts.name: Formal grammar
concepts.summary: A complete description of a language as a compact system of explicit rules.

concepts.name: Political economy
concepts.summary: The systematic study of how wealth is produced, exchanged and distributed, treating the economy as a system with regularities of its own.

concepts.name: Flute
concepts.summary: A pipe with finger holes that sounds a chosen series of pitches when blown.

concepts.name: Musical notation
concepts.summary: Written signs that record a piece of music so that someone who has never heard it can perform it.

concepts.name: Electronic musical instrument
concepts.summary: An instrument whose sound is generated and shaped by electrical circuits instead of by vibrating strings, air or skins.

concepts.name: Figurative art
concepts.summary: Making images that depict recognisable animals, people or scenes.

concepts.name: Monumental stone sculpture
concepts.summary: Carving and setting up stone figures larger than life, which takes quarrying, transport and organised labour.

concepts.name: Linear perspective
concepts.summary: A geometric method for drawing a scene on a flat surface as it appears from one fixed viewpoint, with receding lines meeting at a vanishing point.

concepts.name: Written literature
concepts.summary: Composing and preserving hymns, stories, proverbs and poems in writing, as works to be copied and read.

concepts.name: Specialist oral tradition
concepts.summary: A trained, often hereditary body of specialists who memorise, perform and pass on a society's long texts, histories and genealogies without writing.

concepts.name: Novel
concepts.summary: A long invented story in prose that follows the inner lives and relations of individual characters.

concepts.name: Scripted theatre
concepts.summary: Actors performing a composed play before an audience, in a set place and by shared conventions.

concepts.name: Board game
concepts.summary: A game of fixed rules played by moving pieces on a marked board.

concepts.name: Chess
concepts.summary: A two-player board game of pure skill between armies of unequal pieces, won by trapping the opposing king.

concepts.name: Team ball game
concepts.summary: An organised contest between sides played with a ball on a purpose-built court or field under shared rules.

concepts.name: Codified sport
concepts.summary: Sport played to written rules set by a governing association, which lets clubs anywhere compete in leagues and championships.

concepts.name: Surfing
concepts.summary: Riding breaking waves on a board for sport.

concepts.name: Cinema
concepts.summary: Showing photographed moving pictures to an assembled, paying audience.

concepts.name: Video game
concepts.summary: A game played by controlling images on an electronic display.
